pr_body:
# Objective

Adds a new `Monitor` component representing a winit `MonitorHandle` that can be used to spawn new windows and check for system monitor information.

Closes #12955.

## Solution

For every winit event, check available monitors and spawn them into the world as components.

## Testing

TODO:
- [x] Test plugging in and unplugging monitor during app runtime
- [x] Test spawning a window on a second monitor by entity id
- [ ] Since this touches winit, test all platforms

---

## Changelog

- Adds a new `Monitor` component that can be queried for information about available system monitors.

## Migration Guide

- `WindowMode` variants now take a `MonitorSelection`, which can be set to `MonitorSelection::Primary` to mirror the old behavior.

Made a small example, feel free to pull in this commit if you think it's useful: https://github.com/killercup/bevy/commit/62baba90c2bc92fda8041ec6b3f5112db48cd7c0

> I haven't tested this, and I'm not sure how to easily do that.

Mostly we just need to check that things compile and run on most platforms, but I'm also going to do some experiments with un/replugging monitors just to make sure that we correctly spawn and despawn these as that happens. 

> Made a small example, feel free to pull in this commit if you think it's useful: [killercup@62baba9](https://github.com/killercup/bevy/commit/62baba90c2bc92fda8041ec6b3f5112db48cd7c0)

Thanks! Will absolutely take this.
would it be possible in the example to open a window in each monitor detected, displaying that monitor information?

> would it be possible in the example to open a window in each monitor detected, displaying that monitor information?

That's a great idea, I noticed we don't have any examples of that anywhere. Will add.

Okay, so in working through this new example, I realized that we really needed to also make the window's mode configurable by a monitor selection, as this is actually the correct way to open a window on a particular monitor in winit. Setting the window's position worked sometimes in my experiments, but depended a lot on whether the app was starting on the primary or secondary monitor. 

I did confirm that plugging and unplugging monitors works.

I just tested the example on macOS 14.4.1 with two monitors and ran into a crash. Are the following issues known? Technically these are not introduced by this PR but it is surfaced (to me at least) by the new example. I'll gladly open a new issue for this if we want to land this for now.

## Scaling factor

It opened two fullscreen windows, with the one on the secondary monitor (laptop screen) not having the right scaling in the UI despite it being reported as 2.0.

Maybe related to https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/13702?

## Panic on monitor disconnect

The panic comes from [this assert](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/v0.30.1/src/platform_impl/macos/window_delegate.rs#L1377-L1380) in winit's `WindowDelegate::set_fullscreen` and the error code is `1001`, which is [`CGError.illegalArgument`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coregraphics/cgerror/illegalargument). The call stack points to [`Window::drop`](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/v0.30.1/src/window.rs#L55-L57). It seems specific to the window being `Fullscreen::Exclusive`, and the `native_identifier` of the monitor is not valid (anymore).

## Blank screen on monitor connect

When starting with just the laptop screen, I get one fullscreen window. Plugging in the external screen, there is now a window on the new primary screen, but the laptop screen is black (blank, not grey!). I cannot switch to any other application, but <kbd>Cmd+Q</kbd> works to exit the example app.

## Test: Borderless fullscreen

```diff

@@ -42,7 +42,7 @@ fn update(
             .spawn((
                 Window {
                     title: name.clone(),
-                    mode: WindowMode::Fullscreen(MonitorSelection::Entity(entity)),
+                    mode: WindowMode::BorderlessFullscreen(MonitorSelection::Entity(entity)),
                     position: WindowPosition::Centered(MonitorSelection::Entity(entity)),
                     ..default()
                 },
```

issue_context.title: Expose `winit::monitor` as queryable component
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

Currently, Bevy allows window creation via [`MonitorSelection`](https://docs.rs/bevy/0.13.2/bevy/window/enum.MonitorSelection.html), but does not expose any information about what monitors are available. For [Nannou](https://github.com/nannou-org/nannou/), we need to expose monitor metadata to allows users to programmatically select the monitor. Creative coding applications tend have much more demanding multi-window/multi-monitor setups, and so this information is generally useful.

## What solution would you like?

We'd like to implement the following features:
- Expose the data provided by [`winit::monitor::MonitorHandle`](https://docs.rs/winit/0.29.15/winit/monitor/struct.MonitorHandle.html) as a user queryable component.
- Allow creation of a window via a monitor's `Entity`.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

N/A

## Additional context

N/A
comments: Sounds reasonable :) I think that these should be monitor entities, and work just like window entities with a synchronization step.

review_comments: This also seems to update the list of known monitors (despite the name :D), maybe add this in a doc comment?

Yeah, honestly, this should probably be renamed. `create_windows` indicates that we are spawning windows on the winit side, but in this case we are actually synchronizing in the other direction. I'll definitely add some docs to clarify at least, just thought to keep the naming the same as it's at least a conceptually similar hook between the bevy world and winit.

How often is this called? If performance/allocations are not a blocker, a `BTreeSet<MonitorHandle>` might be nicer to use, you can then also build one from `monitors.monitors` and use `.difference()` to find the monitors no longer present.

It's called very frequently, but in 98% of cases the user will only ever have a single monitor, so I doubt the performance differential is very much either way. I'm going to play around with one of the btree varients and see if that helps clean some of the code up. 👍

Ah, okay, then maybe using smallvec would make a difference here? Not sure there is much need to optimize this too much without profiling but seeing a heap allocation for a list of 1-10 bools is sticking out :D
The code is much cleaner with the btree, so I think it's a good idea!
Resources being reflect is mildly useful, but IME not nearly as important as for things that want to be inspected or serialized.
If you're going with it above, also add `#[doc(alias = "WinitPrimaryScreen")]`/`#[doc(alias = "WinitPrimaryDisplay")]` here :)
